source.title: Bootstrapping ViTs: Towards Liberating Vision Transformers from Pre-training
source.authors: Hao-Fei Zhang; Jiarui Duan; Mengqi Xue; Jie Song; Li Sun; Ming-Li Song

record.tranche_reason: Tests training-from-scratch ViT and CNN generalization on image-classification datasets with limited labeled data, comparing an inductive-bias training method and model settings.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test accuracy for its own ViT, agent CNN, joint/shared training, optimizer, and loss ablations. It does not test random-label memorization, width beyond interpolation, the listed optimizer or batch-size comparisons, dropout, sharpness-gap measures, or removing memorized examples. Cited results are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses convolutional inductive biases to improve its ViT training method. Its comparisons concern Transformers, CNN agents, and training ablations, not fully connected image classifiers as V3 specifies. None of its own results tests V1–V8; optimizer choices differ across architectures, and SAM accuracy alone does not test V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' conclusion: CNN-assisted training is intended to transfer inductive biases, speed convergence, and improve ViT accuracy without pre-training. Their broad statement about outperforming conventional CNNs needs qualification when describing results: joint ViT-B reaches 49.73% versus ResNet50's 50.86% at 10% ImageNet labels, and shared-weight variants also fall below conventional CNNs in several settings.
record.recipe_differences: The paper trains ViTs jointly with a corresponding CNN agent using intermediate-feature supervision and mutual distillation, with optional shared weights. It evaluates test accuracy, not random-label fitting or train-test gaps.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset, labeled-data fraction, weight sharing, agent architecture, loss terms, feature-supervision decay, adaptive function, and hyperparameters affect reported accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Joint training with a CNN agent improves ViT test accuracy: ViT-S rises from 87.32% to 95.14% on CIFAR-10 and from 61.25% to 76.19% on CIFAR-100. ImageNet ViT-B rises from 16.60% to 36.01%, 28.11% to 49.73%, and 63.40% to 71.36% with 5%, 10%, and 50% labels.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training a vision Transformer jointly with a CNN agent using feature supervision and mutual distillation can improve limited-data image-classification accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Feature-only supervision reaches 74.94% versus 67.16% for mutual learning alone; both reach 76.19%. Removing feature-supervision decay lowers feature-only accuracy to 73.59% and both-loss accuracy to 75.15%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The accuracy benefit of CNN-assisted ViT training depends on its supervision terms and decay strategy.

fits_no_version.finding: CNN agents outperform standalone ViTs in the reported limited-data settings, but the comparison uses attention-based Transformers rather than fully connected classifiers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the tested recipes, CNNs can outperform standalone vision Transformers trained from scratch with limited image data.

record.problems: The reported results are test accuracies, not training accuracies or train-test gaps. No random-label capacity check is reported. The supplied text has an internal discrepancy: Table 1 gives CIFAR-100 ViT-S improvement as +14.94, whereas the prose says 14.49%. Table 3 reports 50% labeled samples while the setup passage mentions 1%, 5%, and 10%.
record.rows_left_out: None; 43 rows retained, below the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and the natural-label versus random-label held-out comparison.
Width increases beyond the width required for zero training error, with training to convergence.
CNN versus fully connected image classifiers, local-connectivity attribution, learned sparse local connections, and convolution-derived initialization of fully connected networks.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparisons on the same workload, including tuning, switching, and weight-decay remedies.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove large-batch penalties.
Dropout addition, dropout strength, training-set-size dependence, and joint dropout/weight-decay removal.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization-gap correlations, and rankings against norm- and margin-based measures.
Identification and removal of memorized examples, retraining, and comparison with random removal.

record.verdict_notes: All rows retain versions ["none"]. Their cannot_determine states concern the listed claim versions, not the readability of the reported accuracies. The study's method-performance and ablation rows belong under fits_no_version. Missing is empty because no omitted result tests V1–V8.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or comparison of natural-label and random-label held-out accuracy.
No width sweep beyond the threshold for zero training error.
Does not compare matched convolutional and fully connected networks, nor isolate local connectivity as the cause of an advantage.
No adaptive-optimizer versus SGD generalization comparison; optimizer choice differs across model families.
No batch-size comparison or fixed-epoch large-batch penalty test.
No dropout or weight-decay removal comparison.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or comparison of generalization-gap measures.
No memorized-example identification, removal, or retraining test.
